skill.name: quality-reviewer
skill.description: Reviews DevPrep AI frontend code against project standards using Bash quality checks, documentation, and examples for TypeScript, imports, architecture, naming, complexity, and file size.
skill.summary: Runs DevPrep AI quality checks and explains fixes for frontend code standards.
skill.author: ArieGoldkin

security_audit.summary: Most static findings in documentation and examples are false positives from Markdown backticks, example imports, validation examples, and documented skill paths. Confirmed risk remains from bundled Bash scripts, especially npx and npm execution plus project-root traversal in full-review.sh. No prompt injection text was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before any Bash script, npx, or npm command runs, even when quality keywords trigger the skill.
Document that full-review.sh runs local package scripts and limit use to trusted DevPrep AI repositories.
Resolve the project root through a validated argument or current working directory, and fail if it leaves the expected repository.

remediation.issue: Executable mode and read-only review are combined
remediation.suggestion: Separate read-only review guidance from script execution so users can inspect standards without running commands.

content.value_statement: DevPrep AI code can drift from local standards as teams change files. This skill runs targeted checks and explains fixes for size, imports, naming, architecture, ESLint, and TypeScript.
actual_capabilities: Runs quality scripts for file size, complexity, imports, architecture, naming, ESLint, and TypeScript checks.
Explains DevPrep AI TypeScript standards, path alias rules, and the six-folder frontend structure.
Shows examples of compliant code, intentional violations, and refactored component structure.
Suggests fixes for oversized files, deep relative imports, missing interface prefixes, and complex functions.
Supports both single-check workflows and a full review workflow for trusted DevPrep AI repositories.
limitations: The checks are tailored to the DevPrep AI frontend structure and aliases.
The Bash scripts expect a frontend directory with npm and ESLint tooling available.
The skill is not a general security scanner or dependency audit tool.
Running the scripts on untrusted repositories can execute local project tooling.

use_cases.title: Check a frontend change
use_cases.description: Run the targeted quality checks before submitting DevPrep AI frontend work.

use_cases.title: Enforce team standards
use_cases.description: Use the documented rules to keep imports, naming, file size, and architecture consistent.

use_cases.title: Guide AI-assisted refactoring
use_cases.description: Ask an assistant to split large files and reduce complexity using the provided examples.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Quality Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review before opening a pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current DevPrep AI frontend changes for file size, imports, naming, and TypeScript issues. Ask before running Bash commands.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Failed Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow after a script reports violations.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the quality check failures in plain language and list the smallest safe fixes for each issue.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor an Oversized Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced cleanup for files over the project line limit.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor the oversized component using the DevPrep AI split pattern. Separate UI, hooks, types, and helpers where appropriate.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a CI Quality Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a CI quality gate using the available review scripts. Include explicit command confirmation and explain expected failure output.

output_examples.input: Review my recent frontend changes for DevPrep AI standards.
output: A concise status summary for file size, complexity, imports, architecture, naming, ESLint, and TypeScript.
A list of violations with affected files and practical fix guidance.
A note when Bash command confirmation is required before checks run.

output_examples.input: This component is too large and hard to maintain.
output: A refactoring plan that separates UI rendering, hook logic, type definitions, and helpers.
A checklist for preserving behavior while reducing file size and function complexity.

output_examples.input: Why did the import check fail?
output_examples.output: An explanation of the deep relative import rule, the preferred path aliases, and the files that need updates.

best_practices: Run executable checks only in trusted DevPrep AI repositories.
Ask for confirmation before invoking Bash, npx, npm, or full-review scripts.
Review violations first, then apply the smallest changes that satisfy the documented standard.
anti_patterns: Do not run the scripts against unknown repositories with Bash enabled.
Do not treat this skill as a complete security or dependency audit.
Do not bypass failed checks without documenting the project-specific reason.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews DevPrep AI frontend standards for file size, complexity, imports, architecture, naming, ESLint, and TypeScript.

faq.question: Does it work outside DevPrep AI?
faq.answer: It may run elsewhere, but the rules and scripts assume the DevPrep AI frontend layout.

faq.question: Does the skill execute commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Bash scripts and should ask for confirmation before running them.

faq.question: Can it fix violations automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide or make code changes when used by an editing agent, but the scripts mainly report violations.

faq.question: Is this a security scanner?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on code quality standards and does not replace security review.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
